_doc: Plot specs of the Cloud Calc LaTeX library, keyed by formula id (data/latex/100-formulas.md and pi-formulas.md). Merged into assets/latex/formulas.json by gen-formulas.mjs. Per formula: caption (one line: what is plotted), kind (function = the formula itself, illustration = an honest picture of an identity or relation), vars {symbol: [label, default, min, max, step]} (every variable gets a slider and a field; a variable a plot sweeps is also the probe), d2 {x (swept variable), y (second swept variable of a field), n, layers}, d3 {x, y, z (swept variables), n, g, layers}, anim (variable the Animate button drives) and wave {freq, amp, phase} (variables the Wave sliders expose). Layers: 2D line param points scatter hline vline dot field; 3D surface psurface curve points dot quiver platonic. Expressions are the safe language of assets/latex/plot/expr.js (sin, cos, exp, sqrt, sum(i,a,b,body), ...; no eval).

the-pythagorean-theorem.caption: Hypotenuse c = sqrt(a^2 + b^2): c against leg a for the chosen b (2D), and over both legs (3D).

euler-s-identity.caption: e^(i*theta) on the unit circle (2D) and as a helix (theta, cos, sin) (3D); at theta = pi the point is -1, so e^(i pi) + 1 = 0.

euler-s-formula.caption: Re and Im of e^(i k theta) = cos(k theta) + i sin(k theta) against theta (2D), and the helix (theta, cos, sin) (3D); k is the frequency.

the-quadratic-formula.caption: The parabola y = a x^2 + b x + c with its roots where it crosses 0 (2D), and the same polynomial over x and c (3D).

the-binomial-theorem.caption: (x+y)^n against x, and its binomial expansion term by term (they coincide) (2D); (x+y)^n over x and y (3D).

euler-s-polyhedral-formula.caption: Illustration: for the five regular polyhedra the point (V+F, E) lies on the line E = V+F-2 (2D); the chosen polyhedron drawn in 3D.

s: Solid (1 tetra, 2 cube, 3 octa, 4 dodeca, 5 icosa)

the-law-of-cosines.caption: Side c = sqrt(a^2+b^2-2ab cos C) against the angle C (2D), and over a and C (3D).

the-law-of-sines.caption: Side a = 2R sin A against the angle A for the circumradius R (2D), and over R and A (3D).

heron-s-formula.caption: Triangle area A against side a (gaps where no triangle exists) (2D), and over a and b (3D).

the-prime-number-theorem.caption: The prime counting function pi(x) against x/ln x (2D); the curve (x, pi(x), x/ln x) (3D).

the-basel-problem-euler-s-sum.caption: Partial sums of 1/k^s with N terms against N, and the limit zeta(s) (2D); the term magnitude N^-s over N and s (3D).

the-riemann-zeta-function.caption: zeta(s) from the sum over n and from the Euler product over primes up to N (2D); the partial sum over s and N (3D).

de-moivre-s-formula.caption: Re and Im of (cos t + i sin t)^n = cos(nt) + i sin(nt) (2D); the helix (t, cos nt, sin nt) (3D); n is the frequency.

stirling-s-approximation.caption: The ratio n! / (sqrt(2 pi n) (n/e)^n) tends to 1 (2D); the ratio with the 1/(12n) correction over n and m (3D).

the-chudnovsky-algorithm-for.caption: Correct digits of pi after N terms of the Chudnovsky series (2D); the log10 term size over k and the constant b (3D).

the-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus.caption: f(x) = x^3/6 - x with f'(x), and f(x) - f(a) = integral of f' from a to x; the bounds a and b marked (2D); f(b) - f(a) over a and b (3D).

the-formal-definition-of-the-derivative.caption: The difference quotient of sin with step h against the true derivative cos (2D); the quotient over x and h (3D).

integration-by-parts.caption: With u = x, dv = cos(kx) dx: u*v, the integral of v du, and their difference, the integral of u dv (2D); the integral of u dv over x and k (3D).

taylor-series-expansion.caption: sin x and its Taylor polynomial of degree N about 0 (2D); the error of the polynomial over x and N (3D).

the-continuous-fourier-transform.caption: A Gaussian f(x) of width s and its Fourier transform, which is a Gaussian of width 1/s (2D); the transform over xi and s (3D).

the-inverse-fourier-transform.caption: A Gaussian rebuilt from its spectrum cut off at band B, against the exact Gaussian (2D); the rebuilt function over x and B (3D).

the-laplace-transform.caption: F(s) = 1/(s+a) for f(t) = e^(-at), and the same integral done numerically (2D); F over s and a (3D).

the-cauchy-schwarz-inequality.caption: (u.v)^2 stays below |u|^2 |v|^2 as the angle between the vectors turns (2D); both sides over the angle and |v| (3D).

cauchy-s-integral-formula.caption: Illustration: the contour circle and the point a inside it (2D); |1/(z-a)| over the complex plane, the pole at a (3D, clipped).

cauchy-s-residue-theorem.caption: Illustration: the contour and two simple poles at +-p (2D); |1/((z-p)(z+p))| over the complex plane (3D, clipped).

the-divergence-gauss-ostrogradsky-theore.caption: Illustration: the field F = (x, k y) with the boundary circle of radius R (2D); the field F = (x, k y, z) as arrows in a cube (3D). Divergence is 1+k (2D).

stokes-theorem.caption: Illustration: the rotating field F = k(-y, x) with a boundary loop of radius R (2D); the same field in 3D. Its curl is 2k.

green-s-theorem.caption: Illustration: the field (L, M) = (-k y, x y) with a loop of radius R (2D); the integrand dM/dx - dL/dy = y + k over the plane (3D).

the-heat-equation.caption: The spreading Gaussian solution u(x,t) = exp(-x^2/(4at)) / sqrt(4 pi a t) at time t, with an earlier snapshot (2D); the space-time surface (3D).

the-classical-wave-equation.caption: A travelling wave u = A sin(2 pi f (x/v - t) + phase) at time t (2D); the space-time surface (3D). Change the frequency f.

bayes-theorem.caption: The posterior P(A|B) against the prior P(A), with the prior itself dashed (2D); the posterior over the prior and the false positive rate (3D).

the-normal-gaussian-distribution.caption: The normal density and its cumulative distribution (2D); the density over x and the spread (3D).

the-central-limit-theorem.caption: The density of the standardised mean of n uniform variables (Irwin-Hall) against the standard normal (2D); that density over z and n (3D).

the-poisson-distribution.caption: The Poisson probabilities P(X = k) as stems for the rate lambda (2D); the probability over k and lambda (3D).

the-binomial-distribution.caption: The binomial probabilities P(X = k) as stems for n trials and success rate p (2D); the probability over k and p (3D).

variance-of-a-random-variable.caption: Var(X) = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2 for a binomial count, from the two sides (identical) against p (2D); the variance over p and n (3D).

covariance.caption: A cloud of 300 correlated pairs with covariance rho*s1*s2 (2D); their joint density over the plane (3D).

pearson-correlation-coefficient.caption: The same cloud with its regression line y = rho*(s2/s1)*x (2D); the joint density for sigma_x, sigma_y and rho (3D).

shannon-entropy.caption: Binary entropy H(p) in bits (2D); the entropy of a three-outcome distribution (p1, p2, 1-p1-p2) (3D).

kullback-leibler-divergence.caption: D(P||Q) and D(Q||P) for Bernoulli P (p) and Q (q) against q: not symmetric (2D); D(P||Q) over p and q (3D).

chebyshev-s-inequality.caption: The bound 1/k^2 against the true tail of a normal and of a Laplace variable (2D); the slack of the bound over k and the mix m (3D).

weak-law-of-large-numbers.caption: Running mean of n deterministic pseudo-random coin flips (rate p) settling at p (2D); the distance |mean - p| over n and the seed (3D).

the-black-scholes-equation.caption: European call value from the Black-Scholes solution against the price S, with the payoff (2D); the value over S and the time to expiry (3D).

newton-s-second-law-of-motion.caption: F = m a against the acceleration, and the momentum gained after t seconds (2D); F over m and a (3D).

newton-s-law-of-universal-gravitation.caption: Attraction F = G m1 m2 / r^2 against the distance r (masses in 1e24 kg, r in 1e8 m, force in 1e18 N at the default scale) (2D); F over r and m1 (3D).

kinetic-energy.caption: E = m v^2 / 2 against the speed, and p^2/(2m) from the momentum (identical) (2D); E over v and m (3D).

gravitational-potential-energy-uniform-f.caption: U = m g h against the height for the field g (2D); U over h and g (3D, from the Moon to Jupiter).

general-gravitational-potential-energy.caption: U(r) = -G M m / r against the distance (M in 1e24 kg, r in 1e6 m, U in MJ) (2D); U over r and M (3D).

hooke-s-law.caption: Spring force F = -k x and its stored energy k x^2 / 2 against the extension (2D); F over x and k (3D).

simple-harmonic-angular-frequency.caption: The oscillation x(t) = A cos(omega t) with omega = sqrt(k/m) (2D); omega over k and m (3D). Change the stiffness to change the frequency.

period-of-a-simple-pendulum.caption: Period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) against the length L, with the large-angle correction (2D); T over L and g (3D).

kepler-s-third-law-harmonic-law.caption: Orbital period T = sqrt(a^3 / M) in years against the semi-major axis (AU) around a star of M suns, with the planets for M = 1 (2D); T over a and M (3D).

the-work-energy-theorem.caption: Force F(x) = F0 + c x and the work W(x) = F0 x + c x^2 / 2, which is the kinetic energy gained (2D); W over x and c (3D).

the-euler-lagrange-equation.caption: The path q(t) = A cos(omega t + phase) that satisfies the Euler-Lagrange equation for L = m qdot^2/2 - k q^2/2, with qdot (2D); the curve (t, q, qdot) (3D).

hamilton-s-canonical-equations.caption: Pendulum phase plane: the flow field (q̇, ṗ) with the level curve of H = p^2/2m - m gl cos q for energy E (2D); H over q and p (3D).

the-first-law-of-thermodynamics.caption: Ideal-gas P-V diagram: the isotherm (heat in = work out) and the adiabat (no heat) from the same start (2D); P over V and T (3D).

the-second-law-of-thermodynamics-clausiu.caption: Entropy created by moving heat Q from a hot body to a cold one, Q (1/Tc - 1/Th), against Tc: negative when the direction is forbidden (2D); over Tc and Th (3D).

boltzmann-s-entropy-formula.caption: S/k = ln(Omega) for N two-state particles with a fraction f up, Omega = C(N, fN) (2D); S/k over f and N (3D).

the-ideal-gas-law.caption: Pressure P = n R T / V against the volume at T and at 2T (2D); P over V and T (3D). P in kPa, V in litres.

carnot-engine-thermal-efficiency.caption: Efficiency 1 - Tc/Th against Tc, below zero where Tc exceeds Th (2D); over Tc and Th (3D).

maxwell-boltzmann-speed-distribution.caption: Speed distribution f(v) of a gas of molar mass M (g/mol) at temperature T (2D); f over v and T (3D).

gibbs-free-energy.caption: dG = dH - T dS against T: the reaction is spontaneous where it is below 0 (2D); dG over T and dS (3D). kJ and kJ/K.

enthalpy-definition.caption: H = U + P V against the volume at fixed U and P (2D); H over V and P (3D). kPa and litres give joules.

the-stefan-boltzmann-law.caption: Radiated power per area j = eps sigma T^4 against T (2D); j over T and the emissivity (3D). W/m^2.

planck-s-law-of-blackbody-radiation.caption: Spectral radiance of a black body against the wavelength (micrometres) at temperature T (2D); over wavelength and T (3D).

gauss-s-law-electrostatics.caption: Field of a point charge q: arrows pointing out of a positive charge, in to a negative one (2D); the field in a cube (3D).

gauss-s-law-for-magnetism.caption: Field of a magnetic dipole in the x-z plane: the lines close on themselves (2D); the dipole field in a cube (3D).

faraday-s-law-of-electromagnetic-inducti.caption: Induced electric field circulating around a changing uniform magnetic field of radius R (2D); the field in a cube (3D).

the-ampe-re-maxwell-law.caption: Magnetic field circling a wire carrying current I (2D); the field around the wire in a cube (3D).

the-lorentz-force-law.caption: Path of a charge in crossed fields E and B, a cycloid in the plane (2D) with the drift along B in 3D. w is the cyclotron frequency.

coulomb-s-law.caption: Force F = k q1 q2 / r^2 against the distance (charges in µC, r in cm, F in N; negative = attraction) (2D); F over r and q1 (3D).

ohm-s-law-microscopic-and-macroscopic.caption: V = I R against the current for resistance R, and for 2R (2D); V over I and R (3D). The microscopic J = sigma E is the same line.

snell-s-law-of-refraction.caption: Refraction angle against the incidence angle; the curve stops at the critical angle where light is totally reflected (2D); the angle over theta1 and n2 (3D).

the-poynting-vector.caption: A plane wave: E, B and the energy flow S = E B at time t (2D); S over position and time (3D). Change the frequency f.

speed-of-light-from-electromagnetic-cons.caption: Speed of light 1/sqrt(eps mu) in a medium, in 1e8 m/s, against the relative permittivity (2D); over eps_r and mu_r (3D).

mass-energy-equivalence.caption: E = m c^2 in units of 1e16 J against the mass in kg (2D); E over the mass and a scale of c (3D).

cf: c as a fraction of its value

relativistic-energy-momentum-relation.caption: Total energy sqrt((pc)^2 + (mc^2)^2) in MeV against pc, with the massless line and the kinetic energy (2D); E over pc and mc^2 (3D).

the-lorentz-factor.caption: gamma against v/c, rising without bound near 1 (2D); gamma over the velocity components (bx, by) inside the unit disc (3D).

relativistic-time-dilation.caption: Time between two ticks seen by an observer: dt/sqrt(1-b^2) against v/c (2D); over v/c and the proper time (3D).

relativistic-length-contraction.caption: Length L0 sqrt(1-b^2) seen by an observer against v/c (2D); over v/c and the rest length (3D).

einstein-s-field-equations-of-general-re.caption: Illustration: the time-time metric -(1 - rs/r) of a mass against r (2D); the embedding surface (Flamm paraboloid) of the space around it (3D).

the-schwarzschild-radius.caption: rs = 2GM/c^2 in km against the mass in suns (2D); the horizon sphere of the chosen mass (3D).

the-spacetime-invariant-interval.caption: Illustration: the light cone and the curves of constant interval s2 in an x-ct diagram (2D); the interval x^2 + y^2 - (ct)^2 over the plane (3D).

the-planck-einstein-relation.caption: Photon energy E = h nu in eV against the frequency in THz (2D); the energy of N photons over nu and N (3D).

the-de-broglie-wavelength.caption: Wavelength lambda = h/(m v) in nm against the speed (1e6 m/s) for a particle of m electron masses (2D); over v and m (3D).

the-time-dependent-schro-dinger-equation.caption: A free Gaussian wave packet: density |psi|^2 spreading and moving, with an illustrative Re psi (2D); the density over x and t (3D). hbar = m = 1.

the-time-independent-schro-dinger-equati.caption: Particle in a box of width L: the eigenfunction psi_n and its density, with E_n = n^2 pi^2/(2L^2) (2D); psi over x and n (3D).

heisenberg-s-uncertainty-principle.caption: The smallest allowed sigma_p = hbar/(2 sigma_x) and that of the oscillator level n against sigma_x (2D); sigma_x sigma_p - hbar/2 over both (3D). hbar = 1.

the-dirac-equation.caption: The relativistic dispersion E = +-sqrt(p^2 + m^2) with the gap 2m (2D); both energy sheets over (px, py) (3D). c = 1.

bohr-orbit-radius.caption: Bohr radii r_n = a0 n^2 / Z (nm) as stems (2D); the first four orbits drawn as circles (3D).

the-rydberg-formula.caption: Spectral line wavelengths (nm) for the lower level n1 as n2 grows (2D); wavelength over n1 and n2 (3D).

the-fermi-dirac-distribution.caption: Occupation 1/(exp((en-mu)/kT)+1) against the energy, with the zero-temperature step (2D); occupation over e and kT (3D).

the-incompressible-navier-stokes-equatio.caption: The Taylor-Green vortex, an exact solution, decaying with viscosity nu: velocity arrows at time t (2D); its vorticity surface (3D).

the-fluid-continuity-equation.caption: A density pulse carried along by a flow u: rho(x,t) = rho0(x - u t) (2D); the pulse in space-time (3D).

bernoulli-s-principle.caption: Pressure p2 (kPa) in a pipe whose cross-section changes by the ratio a = A2/A1 (2D); p2 over a and the inflow speed (3D).

the-arrhenius-equation.caption: Rate constant k = A exp(-Ea/RT) against T (2D); k over T and Ea (3D). Ea in kJ/mol.

the-nernst-equation.caption: Cell potential E = E0 - (RT/zF) ln Q against log10 Q (2D); E over log10 Q and the temperature (3D).

the-hubble-lemai-tre-law.caption: Recession speed v = H0 d against the distance (Mpc), with the two measured H0 values dashed (2D); v over d and H0 (3D). km/s.

the-first-friedmann-equation.caption: Expansion rate H(a)/H0 = sqrt(Om a^-3 + Ok a^-2 + OL) against the scale factor (2D); over a and Om (3D). Ok = 1 - Om - OL.

the-logistic-map.caption: The bifurcation diagram: late iterates of x -> r x (1-x) for each r (2D); the iterate x_n over r and the step n (3D).

pi-leibniz-series.caption: Partial sums of the Leibniz series 4(1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - ...) closing in on pi (2D); the Gregory partial sum over N and the argument z, z = 1 being Leibniz (3D).

pi-nilakantha-series.caption: Partial sums of 3 + 4/(2·3·4) - 4/(4·5·6) + ... (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-wallis-product.caption: Partial Wallis products 2·Π 4k^2/(4k^2-1) rising to pi (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-viete-product.caption: Viete's product: pi = 2 / Π cos(pi/2^(k+1)), the nested radicals, after N factors (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-machin-formula.caption: Machin: 16 arctan(1/5) - 4 arctan(1/239) with N series terms each (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-bbp-formula.caption: BBP: pi = Σ 16^-k (4/(8k+1) - 2/(8k+4) - 1/(8k+5) - 1/(8k+6)) after N terms (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-ramanujan-1914-series.caption: Ramanujan's 1914 series: each term adds about 8 digits (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-gauss-legendre-iteration.caption: Gauss-Legendre: the digits double with every AGM step; N steps (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-zeta-4.caption: pi estimated as (90 Σ 1/k^4)^(1/4) after N terms (2D); the term size 1/k^s over N and s (3D).

pi-gaussian-integral.caption: The Gaussian e^(-x^2) and the area -x..x under it, sqrt(pi) erf(x), approaching sqrt(pi) (2D); the surface e^(-(x^2+y^2)) whose volume is pi (3D).

pi-circle-area.caption: Area of the circle pi r^2 against r, with the area of an inscribed n-gon (2D); the n-gon area over r and n approaching pi r^2 (3D).

pi-circle-circumference.caption: Circumference 2 pi r against r, with the perimeter of an inscribed n-gon (2D); the perimeter over r and n (3D).

pi-buffon-s-needle.caption: Buffon: pi estimated as 2 l n / (t hits) from n pseudo-random needle drops (2D); the drops as points (distance, angle, hit) (3D).

pi-monte-carlo-quarter-circle.caption: Random points in the unit square: those inside the quarter circle (above) and outside, pi ~ 4 inside/total (2D); random points in a cube, the octant of the ball holds pi/6 of them (3D).

pi-stirling-sqrt-2pi.caption: n! / (sqrt(n) (n/e)^n) tends to sqrt(2 pi) (2D); the same ratio with the 1/(12n) correction over n and m (3D).

pi-gregory-arctan-series.caption: arctan x and its Gregory partial sum of N terms, with 4 arctan(1) = pi at x = 1 (2D); the partial-sum error over x and N (3D).

pi-euler-arcsin-series.caption: arcsin x and its series partial sum of N terms, with 6 arcsin(1/2) = pi (2D); the partial sum over x and N (3D).

pi-lambert-continued-fraction.caption: Lambert's continued fraction for tan x cut at depth N against tan x (2D); its error over x and the depth (3D).

pi-ramanujan-sato-series.caption: A Ramanujan-Sato series, 16/pi = Σ (42k+5) C(2k,k)^3 / 2^(12k), after N terms: each term adds almost two digits (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).

pi-euler-arctan-identity.caption: arctan a + arctan((1-a)/(1+a)) = pi/4 for every a: the two parts and their constant sum (2D); arctan x + arctan y with the line where the sum is pi/4 (3D).

pi-euler-sine-product.caption: sin(pi x) and Euler's product pi x Π (1 - x^2/n^2) over n <= N (2D); the product over x and N (3D).

pi-gamma-half.caption: The gamma function with Gamma(1/2) = sqrt(pi) marked (2D); the beta function B(x, y) with B(1/2, 1/2) = pi (3D).

pi-reflection-formula.caption: Gamma(z) Gamma(1-z) against pi / sin(pi z): the same curve (2D); the product times sin(pi y) over z and y, equal to pi along y = z (3D).

pi-archimedes-polygons.caption: Archimedes: for an n-gon the inscribed n sin(pi/n) and circumscribed n tan(pi/n) half-perimeters bracket pi (2D); the bracket width over n (3D).

pi-madhava-series.caption: Madhava: pi = sqrt(12) Σ (-1/3)^k / (2k+1) after N terms (2D); the curve (N, estimate, correct digits) (3D).
